name: TKG noise (color background shift)
plain: Shifts selected channels of the start noise so a higher or lower fraction of values are positive, biasing the background to a color. A Gaussian mask keeps the center unshifted, so the subject stays neutral and the background takes the color.
math:
For c with sign s: repeat ε_c += δ·s until frac(ε_c>0) ≥ frac₀ + shift·s (δ=0.1, shift=0.11).
G = exp(−(x²+y²)/(2·0.5²)), upsampled from grid_factor.
ε' = ε_shift·(1−G) + ε·G. Color table maps names to SD1 channel signs (green [0,1,1,0]).

props.distribution: standard normal with a channel mean shift outside center

label: from code
surprise: The loop test is one-sided (new_ratio ≥ target). For sign −1 the ratio falls but stays above target−, so it stops after a single δ step: negative channels move far less than positive ones.
